name: Microsoft 365
contracting_entity: Microsoft Corporation (EU/UK contracts via Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited)
storage: UK data centres for tenants signed up in the UK; EU data centres for tenants signed up in the EU. Covers Exchange mail, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams chat and Copilot. Teams: for a UK tenant, chats are stored at rest in the UK under Microsoft's Product Terms, and EU tenants get EU storage; meeting recordings are saved to the recorder's OneDrive, which follows the same rules. Copilot: prompts and responses are stored in the organisation's tenant (Exchange), so they follow the tenant's data location. EU tenants are covered by the EU Data Boundary, with exceptions. UK in-country processing for Copilot was promised from late 2025, later adjusted to the end of 2026.
plans: All commercial plans, including Business Basic and Business Standard, based on the country chosen at sign-up. The same applies to Teams and to Copilot Chat on any work or school tenant in the UK or EU. Advanced Data Residency is a paid add-on for stronger commitments.
ai_detail: Microsoft states prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train foundation LLMs, including those used by Copilot. This applies to Copilot Chat included with business plans and paid Microsoft 365 Copilot. Optional feedback may be used to improve the service. This does not cover the consumer Microsoft Copilot app used with a personal Microsoft account.
nonprofit_offer: Business Basic is free for eligible non-profits, Business Standard and Business Premium are discounted, and Copilot Chat is included.
note: Your data stays in the UK or EU only if the tenant was set up with a UK or EU country, so check the data location in the admin centre. If you had the free Business Premium grant, check you moved users before it expired, or you risk losing data. Teams recordings are saved in the OneDrive of the person who pressed record, so check where they end up when that person leaves.
note_more: Since 17 April 2026 Microsoft can process EU tenants' Copilot requests outside the EU at busy times (flex routing) unless an admin turns this off. Anthropic models and Bing web search in Copilot also sit outside the EU Data Boundary, so check these settings in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

name: Google Workspace
contracting_entity: Google LLC (EMEA customers usually contract with Google Cloud EMEA Limited, Ireland)
storage: No location commitment by default. Business Standard and above can set a data region policy to Europe (EU); Business Starter and the free Nonprofits edition cannot. There is no UK-only region.
plans: Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus (EU region via admin setting). Not Business Starter or the free Google Workspace for Nonprofits edition.
ai_detail: Google states Workspace does not use customer data to train models without the customer's prior permission or instruction. The Privacy Hub says this applies to qualifying editions.
nonprofit_offer: Google Workspace for Nonprofits is free; Business Standard and Business Plus are discounted, through Google for Nonprofits.
note: On the free Nonprofits edition or Business Starter you cannot choose where your data is stored. To keep data in Europe you need Business Standard or higher and must set the data region to Europe yourself.

name: Dropbox
contracting_entity: Dropbox, Inc. (outside North America: Dropbox International Unlimited Company, Ireland)
storage: US data centres by default. Teams can ask to move data to the UK or EU if they meet conditions.
plans: Standard, Advanced, Business, Business Plus or Enterprise teams with at least 10 licences on annual billing; requests reviewed individually
ai_detail: Dropbox says it will not build generative AI models using customer content without consent. Dash uses OpenAI for web search, on by default in chats, and says data sent is not used to train OpenAI models.
note: Your files are stored in the US unless your team has at least 10 licences on annual billing and asks Dropbox to move them. Small teams should assume US storage.

name: IONOS Nextcloud Workspace
contracting_entity: IONOS SE (UK customers contract with IONOS Cloud UK Limited)
storage: IONOS data centres in Germany
plans: All plans
ai_detail: The AI assistant runs on the IONOS AI Model Hub. IONOS says it contractually guarantees company data will never be used to train public AI models.
note: Your data is held in Germany and the software is open source, so you can move to another Nextcloud host. The UK contract is with IONOS Cloud UK Limited, so check which entity is on your agreement.

name: Hetzner Storage Share
storage: Hetzner's own data centre in Falkenstein, Germany. No other location offered.
plans: All plans (NX11, NX21, NX31)
ai_detail: Any AI apps are ones you install yourself from the Nextcloud app store.
note: Files are stored in Germany and are not encrypted by default. Check you can switch on two-factor login for every user.

name: mailbox.org
storage: Own servers in data centres in Berlin, Germany
plans: All plans
note: Mail, calendars and files are stored in Berlin and use open standards, so moving out is straightforward. The service rebranded from mailbox.org to mailbox in September 2025, so look for either name on invoices.

name: Proton
storage: Switzerland primarily. Proton says business data is on servers in Europe under Swiss law. Some infrastructure has been moved to Germany and Norway since 2024 to 2025, but no customer choice of location is stated.
ai_detail: Proton says Proton Scribe does not use content data to train its models, and Lumo keeps no server-side logs and uses zero-access encryption. Scribe is an add-on; Lumo is included in Workspace Premium.
nonprofit_offer: Discount for registered non-profits on business plans, agreed with sales.
note: Data is mainly held in Switzerland, which is outside the UK and EU but has UK and EU adequacy decisions. Most content is end-to-end encrypted, so if you lose your password and recovery details, the data cannot be recovered.

name: Infomaniak kSuite
storage: Infomaniak's own data centres in Switzerland
plans: Unknown.
ai_detail: Infomaniak says data sent to its Euria assistant is neither saved nor used to train AI, and processing stays in its Swiss data centres. Euria runs on open source models.
note: Your data is held in Switzerland, which is outside the UK and EU but has UK and EU adequacy decisions. You can take your data out in standard formats: files over WebDAV, mail over IMAP, contacts as vCard and calendars as ICS. Two-step login is an Infomaniak account setting, so check it is switched on for every staff account. Ask Infomaniak about nonprofit pricing.

name: Tuta
storage: Tuta's own servers in ISO 27001 certified data centres in Germany
plans: All plans
nonprofit_offer: For registered non-profits and schools: email sales with proof of status.
note: Data is stored in Germany and is end-to-end encrypted. You cannot connect ordinary email apps over IMAP, so exporting mail means using Tuta's desktop app.

name: Zoom
storage: Plan assumed: Zoom Workplace Pro. Recordings, transcripts and other customer content are stored in the US by default. Admins on paid plans, including Pro, can move recordings, transcripts, in-meeting chat and whiteboards to Germany, but account and operational data stay in the US.
plans: Paid plans including Pro can set the storage region to Germany for recordings, transcripts, in-meeting chat and whiteboard content. Zoom's fuller EU infrastructure is described for EU Education and Enterprise customers. There is no UK storage region.
ai_detail: Zoom's terms (section 10.2) say it does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like content to train Zoom or third-party AI models. This applies to all plans; no opt-out is needed.
nonprofit_offer: For verified non-profits under a budget limit, verified through Goodstack.
note: Recordings are stored in the US unless an admin changes the data storage location to Germany in account settings. Account data stays in the US either way.

name: Slack
storage: Plan assumed: Pro (free for nonprofits with up to 250 members). Data is stored in the US. Business+ and Enterprise plans can choose data residency in London, Frankfurt, Paris, Stockholm or Zurich, but member profiles, membership details and analytics stay outside the chosen region.
plans: Business+ and Enterprise (London, Frankfurt, Paris, Stockholm, Zurich). Not available on Free or Pro.
ai_detail: Slack analyses customer data (messages, content, files) to train non-generative global models, such as emoji and channel recommendations, on all plans by default. Workspace owners can opt out by emailing feedback@slack.com with the subject 'Slack Global model opt-out request'. Slack says it does not train generative AI models on customer data without opt-in consent.
nonprofit_offer: Pro is free for smaller workspaces, with discounts above that and on Business+, checked through TechSoup.
note: On Pro, messages are stored in the US and private channels and DMs cannot be exported. Slack uses your data for its recommendation models unless an owner emails feedback@slack.com to opt out.

name: WhatsApp
job: Group messaging and messaging with supporters
contracting_entity: WhatsApp LLC (UK users); WhatsApp Ireland Limited (EEA users)
storage: Plan assumed: free personal WhatsApp accounts used for work groups, or the free WhatsApp Business app (not the paid Business Platform API). Messages are end-to-end encrypted and stored on each member's phone; Business app chats are stored on the phone the business number is registered on. WhatsApp keeps undelivered messages and media encrypted on its servers for up to 30 days. Other account data is shared globally within Meta, including the US. No UK or EU storage option exists.
ai_detail: Ordinary messages are end-to-end encrypted and are not used to train Meta AI. Anything sent to Meta AI, including when someone types @Meta AI in a group, is not end-to-end encrypted and can be used under Meta's privacy policy. Advanced Chat Privacy, off by default, disables some Meta AI features in a chat. For the Business app, any AI tools the business connects are governed by their own terms.
note: Work messages live on staff and volunteers' own phones, so the charity has no central copy and cannot control what leaves with them. Anyone typing @Meta AI in a group sends that part of the chat to Meta unencrypted. The Business app is tied to one phone number and one phone, so decide who holds that phone and how chats are kept when staff change.
note_more: UK accounts are provided by WhatsApp LLC in the US.

name: Signal
storage: Plan assumed: the free Signal app. Messages are end-to-end encrypted and stored on members' devices. Signal's servers only queue encrypted messages for offline devices. Its terms say encrypted information and metadata are transferred to the US and other countries. Signal says it can only provide a user's registration date and last connection date.
ai_detail: Signal cannot read message content, which is end-to-end encrypted, and offers no AI features that use it.
note: Signal holds almost no data about you, but the charity has no admin controls or central copy of chats. Switch on Registration Lock with a PIN to stop someone taking over an account.

name: Element (hosted)
storage: Plan assumed: an Element-hosted server (Element Matrix Services / Element Cloud). Element hosts on Amazon Web Services, with its admin server in Amsterdam and deployment server in Stockholm. Customers choose the location of their own server when they set it up.
plans: Location is chosen at set-up for hosted servers. Element's current public pricing page lists only self-hosted plans (Community free for up to 100 users; Enterprise from 100 users), so the small-organisation hosted offer is unclear.
ai_detail: Element says nobody at Element or its processors can access encrypted data.
note: Check which hosting location was picked when your server was set up, and use your own domain so you can move later. Element's published prices now focus on self-hosting.

name: Jitsi Meet (meet.jit.si)
storage: Plan assumed: the free public service at meet.jit.si. Chat is only kept during the meeting, recordings are held for up to 24 hours until uploaded to your Dropbox, and audio and video are not stored. 8x8 stores the account that created each room.
ai_detail: The meet.jit.si privacy supplement says 8x8 uses personal information to deliver and improve the service.
nonprofit_offer: For everyone.
note: meet.jit.si is free and keeps little meeting content. Since August 2023 whoever starts a meeting must sign in with Google, GitHub or Facebook.

name: Mattermost Cloud
storage: Plan assumed: Mattermost Cloud, which is now sold only through Mattermost sales as an annual subscription with a 100-user minimum. Cloud data, including messages, files, logs and backups, is stored in AWS us-east-1 in Virginia, US.
plans: Mattermost says to contact its sales team or a partner for residency outside the US, or to self-host.
ai_detail: Mattermost's AI Agents connect to a language model provider that the admin configures.
nonprofit_offer: Low-cost licence for self-hosted Mattermost Professional, for non-profits that cannot afford a commercial licence. Cloud is reviewed case by case only for non-profits with over 1,000 users.
note: Mattermost Cloud is hosted in the US and needs at least 100 paid users. The nonprofit licence covers self-hosting, which puts the data wherever you host it.

name: Calendly
storage: US. Calendly says it stores user and invitee data in US data centres run by Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services, on all plans.
plans: Plan assumed: all plans (Free, Standard, Teams). Calendly's help page says the storage statement applies to all plans.
ai_detail: Calendly's security page says: 'Calendly does not sell customer data or use customer data to train AI models. Third-party AI providers are prohibited from using customer data to train their models.' Checked 29 September 2026.
nonprofit_offer: Special pricing for qualified non-profits, agreed with Calendly support.
note: Calendly holds your bookings and your invitees' details in the US, so tell people who book with you. You can export your meetings and your contacts as CSV files. Check that covers what you need. Two-factor login is available on all plans, so switch it on for every account. Ask Calendly's sales team about not-for-profit pricing before you assume a discount.

name: ChatGPT
storage: Not stored in the UK or EU by default. Personal plans and ChatGPT Business have no data residency option. ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu customers can choose to store content at rest in Europe or the UK.
plans: ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu and eligible API customers (Europe and UK storage at rest; expanded to more regions in November 2025). Not ChatGPT Business, Free or Plus.
ai_detail: Free, Go, Plus and Pro (personal): chats are used to train models by default. Opt out by turning off 'Improve the model for everyone' in Settings > Data controls, or via the OpenAI Privacy Portal ('Do not train on my content'). Giving thumbs up or down feedback can still send that whole conversation for training. ChatGPT Business (formerly Team), Enterprise, Edu and the API: not used for training by default; an organisation can opt in.
nonprofit_offer: OpenAI for Nonprofits: discounted Business seats after Goodstack verification, and Enterprise discounts for larger non-profits through sales.
note: Personal ChatGPT accounts train on your chats unless each person turns this off, so staff should not use personal accounts for charity work. ChatGPT Business does not train on your data but stores it outside the UK and EU; only Enterprise offers UK or European storage.

name: Claude
storage: Stored in the US on all Claude plans. Processing may be routed to the US, Europe, Asia and Australia. No UK or EU storage option for Claude Team or Enterprise.
ai_detail: Free, Pro and Max (consumer): since 28 August 2025 each user chooses whether chats and coding sessions are used for training; existing users had to decide by 8 October 2025. If allowed, data is kept for up to five years; if not, the usual 30-day retention applies. Change it any time in Settings > Privacy (model improvement setting); incognito chats are never used. Team, Enterprise, API, Government and Education: not used for training by default.
nonprofit_offer: Claude for Nonprofits, verified through Goodstack. The page lists US non-profits as eligible.
note: Personal Claude accounts may use chats for training if the person allowed it in the 2025 privacy prompt, so check Settings > Privacy. All Claude data is stored in the US, with no UK or EU storage option on any plan.

name: Google Gemini
storage: Unknown for personal accounts and ordinary Workspace plans. Workspace admins can keep Gemini data in the EU only on Enterprise Plus, Frontline Plus, Education editions or Assured Controls add-ons. The UK is not offered as a separate region.
plans: Workspace Enterprise Plus and Frontline Plus (EU processing and storage), Education Standard and Plus (EU storage only), Assured Controls add-ons. Not Workspace for Nonprofits, Business Starter or personal accounts.
ai_detail: Personal Google account (Gemini app): with Keep Activity on, which is the default, chats and uploads are used to improve Google's services, including training generative AI models, and a subset is reviewed by humans (kept up to 3 years, detached from the account). Turn off Keep Activity or use Temporary chats; chats are then kept for 72 hours and not used for training, unless you send feedback. Gemini in Google Workspace (work or school account): customer data is not used to train models without permission and is not human reviewed.
nonprofit_offer: Included in the free Google Workspace for Nonprofits plan.
note: Staff using Gemini on personal Google accounts have their chats used for training and possibly read by reviewers unless they turn off Keep Activity. Use Gemini through the charity's Workspace account, where your data is not used for training.

name: Mistral Vibe (was Le Chat)
storage: Hosted in the EU by default. Some features may transfer data temporarily outside the EU to listed subprocessors; Enterprise customers can switch some of those features off.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Free: chats are used for training by default; opt out in the admin or privacy settings ('Allow your interactions to be used to train our models') or in the mobile app under Data & Account Controls. Pro: Mistral's pages conflict (the help centre says users are not opted out by default, the product docs say Pro is not trained on by default), so check the toggle. Team: admins can switch training off for the whole organisation; the docs say it is off by default. Enterprise: opted out by default. Thumbs up or down feedback can be used for training on any plan.
note: Le Chat was renamed Vibe on 12 August 2026; accounts and data carried over. Data is hosted in the EU, but check the training toggle in the admin panel, especially on Free and Pro.

name: Otter.ai
storage: US by default. Otter uses Amazon Web Services in the United States and relies on the Data Privacy Framework and Standard Contractual Clauses for UK and EU transfers. There is no UK or EU storage option.
ai_detail: Otter trains its own AI on de-identified audio recordings and on transcripts, which may contain personal information, on all plans. Human review of recordings for training needs the user's permission, which can be changed in account settings. Only Enterprise customers can also opt out of the de-identified data use.
note: Otter trains its AI on de-identified recordings and transcripts of your meetings, and only Enterprise customers can opt out. Data is stored in the US.

name: Fireflies.ai
storage: Stored on servers in the United States and other countries. Enterprise customers can buy private storage at a location they choose.
plans: Enterprise (private storage)
ai_detail: Fireflies says it does not use personal information or meeting content for AI model training and contractually bars its AI vendors from training on it, with zero data retention at those vendors. Applies to all plans.
note: Fireflies does not train AI on your meetings, but recordings and transcripts are stored in the US unless you pay for Enterprise private storage. Tell meeting guests the notetaker is recording.

name: Zoom AI Companion
storage: Follows the region the Zoom account is hosted in. Admins on Pro and above can choose Germany for recordings and some content, but out-of-meeting chat and account data stay in the provisioned region. The UK is not in the storage list.
plans: Pro and above can pick Germany for recordings, transcripts and some content; accounts hosted in the EU use Zoom-managed models (ZM+) to respect data residency.
ai_detail: Zoom says it does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like content to train its own or third-party AI models. For US-hosted accounts AI Companion sends content to third-party models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) under zero data retention terms; admins can ask Zoom Support for Zoom-hosted-only processing (ZMO).
nonprofit_offer: On Workplace Pro and Business, which include AI meeting summaries, verified through Goodstack. Other Zoom products are full price.
note: Zoom does not train AI on your meeting content, but by default AI Companion may send it to third-party AI providers for processing. Ask Zoom which region your account is hosted in and which AI processing option applies.

name: Mailchimp
contracting_entity: The Rocket Science Group LLC (Intuit Mailchimp)
storage: US by default for all customers (assumed plan: Essentials or Standard). No EU or UK hosting option. Transfers rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and UK Extension, with SCCs as fallback.
ai_detail: Terms section 30 lets Mailchimp use generative AI Inputs and Outputs, including Customer Data, for machine learning to develop the AI model and services. Section 17 lets it aggregate and anonymise campaign content for its own use. The terms point to data preferences in account settings.
nonprofit_offer: On marketing plans. Ask before you buy, as it is not applied afterwards.
note: Supporter data is stored in the US and there is no UK or EU hosting option. Check the data preferences in your account settings if you use the AI writing features.

name: Brevo
storage: EU for all customers (assumed plan: Starter). Hosted with OVH in France and Germany and Google Cloud in Belgium.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Terms allow Brevo to use Content and Usage Data to train its AI features, limited to improving the services, in particular fraud, phishing and spam prevention and security. Other AI features can be managed in the Control Center, but fraud and spam detection cannot be switched off. Third-party AI providers only process data to provide the feature.
nonprofit_offer: On paid plans for verified non-profits: contact support with proof of status.
note: Data is held in the EU by default. Brevo can use your content to train its anti-spam and fraud AI, and that cannot be switched off.

name: CleverReach
storage: Germany and the EU for all customers (assumed plan: Basic). The supplier says servers are exclusively in Germany and the EU.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: The AI Content Generator sends your prompt to OpenAI. It is an optional feature on Basic and above.
note: Recipient data stays in Germany and the EU. Full two-factor login is listed only on Enterprise; smaller plans can switch on an emailed PIN code at login under Settings.

name: Beacon CRM
storage: UK by default (assumed plan: Starter). Trust page says data is hosted exclusively in the UK on AWS; the sub-processor list names AWS London and Ireland and Google Cloud London for core storage.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Beacon says Beacon AI cannot access your data and does not use it to train public AI models. The AI provider behind Beacon AI is not named in the sub-processor list.
note: Data is held in the UK. In late July 2026 attackers copied Beacon's customer database backups, affecting over 1,000 charities, so check what Beacon has told you and whether you have acted on it.

name: Salesforce Nonprofit
storage: Depends on the region the org is provisioned in (assumed plan: Power of Us donated Enterprise Edition). Hyperforce runs in the UK, Germany and other countries, and data is generally stored in the country where the org is located. The Hyperforce EU Operating Zone adds stronger EU and Swiss residency commitments but is not offered for the UK. Generative AI features may route data to LLM providers such as OpenAI or Azure.
plans: Hyperforce orgs provisioned in a UK or EU region; EU Operating Zone for EU and Swiss customers
ai_detail: Salesforce says generative AI features are not trained on customer data, but predictive Einstein features can use org data for global models. Since the Spring 2026 release admins can switch this off under Setup > Opt Out of Customer Data Access; most orgs start opted in.
nonprofit_offer: Power of Us: donated Enterprise Edition licences for eligible non-profits.
note: Check your instance location on my.trust.salesforce.com, because storage depends on where your org was set up. Ask your admin to review the Opt Out of Customer Data Access setting, which starts switched to allow data use.

name: CiviCRM
storage: Depends entirely on the host (assumed: hosted by a CiviCRM partner). Self-hosted or partner-hosted data sits wherever that server is. CiviCRM's own Spark hosting lets you choose North America or Europe.
plans: Any host with UK or EU servers; Spark with the Europe option
ai_detail: Core CiviCRM has no supplier AI service that receives your data. Check any AI extensions or host services you add.
nonprofit_offer: Free open-source software. You pay for hosting and support.
note: Where your data lives and whether two-factor login is available depend on your hosting partner and the website system CiviCRM runs on. Ask your host where the servers are and whether you can get a full database copy.

name: Donorfy
storage: EU by default (assumed plan: Starter). Hosted on Microsoft Azure North Europe in Dublin, Ireland. Enterprise can use private cloud hosting.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Donorfy is being linked to The Access Group's Access Evo AI features. Access says Evo AI has zero data retention for training and inputs are never used to improve models. Evo features were switched on automatically from 17 November 2025 and admins can turn them off.
note: Data is held in Ireland. A full export with all fields and attachments costs extra, so ask for the price before you decide to leave.

name: HubSpot
storage: Set at sign-up by the IP address location (assumed plan: free CRM or Starter). HubSpot has an EU data centre in Germany; accounts started in the US data centre can be moved to the EU on any plan. Usage data and some processing still go to the US.
plans: All plans (EU data centre by sign-up location or migration)
ai_detail: HubSpot uses customer data such as CRM activity to train its models by default. Super Admins can switch off 'AI Model Training' under Settings > AI > Access. Opt-out applies from then on only. Accounts with Sensitive Data enabled are opted out.
nonprofit_offer: Only for non-profits registered in North America, Australia and New Zealand. Starter is excluded.
note: Check Account defaults to see which data centre your account uses, as UK sign-ups may land in the US. HubSpot trains AI on your CRM data unless a Super Admin switches it off.

name: ForeningLet
storage: EU only. ForeningLet's data processing agreement says processing takes place 'inden for EUs grænser' (within the EU) and that personal data is never transferred to third countries. Amazon (Ireland) hosts the IT infrastructure.
plans: Base package from 99 kr a month for up to 100 members, before VAT (checked 29 September 2026). The data processing terms apply to all customers.
ai_detail: ForeningLet has an AI assistant that searches the user guide and, depending on user rights, looks up members and invoices. The user guide says: 'Ingen data sendes videre til tredjepart' (no data is sent to third parties) and 'Al behandling kører på servere hos ForeningLet' (all processing runs on ForeningLet's servers).
note: ForeningLet offers a data processing agreement (databehandleraftale) and says data stays in the EU, hosted by Amazon in Ireland. It holds your members' personal data, so check that your organisation has accepted the agreement and that one person is not the only administrator. You can export member lists to Excel or CSV, so do that regularly. Two-factor login is available: an administrator switches it on under Opsætning, Forening, To-faktor-login, and it then applies to all administrators, with a one-time code sent by email.

name: Membersite
storage: Denmark. EG says its Membercare membership system, which includes the Membersite self-service portal, is 'udviklet, hostet og GDPR-sikret i Danmark' (developed, hosted and GDPR-secured in Denmark). The same page also says 'udviklet og hosted i norden' (Nordic), so the exact country is worth confirming.
plans: Membersite is the member self-service part of EG Membercare (packages Basis, Udvidet and Premium). EG prices Membercare by number of members and chosen modules, on a quote. Plan assumed: any Membercare package.
ai_detail: Unknown.
note: Membersite was made by Groupcare, which EG bought in November 2023, and is now sold as part of EG Membercare. EG says the system is hosted in Denmark. Ask EG for its data processing agreement (databehandleraftale). The price is by quote. Ask how you get your member data out if you leave, and whether administrators can use two-step login.

name: JustGiving
storage: Unknown. The privacy policy says some personal data may be stored outside the UK, EU or EEA, and JustGiving is covered by Blackbaud's EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification.
ai_detail: The privacy policy says JustGiving uses machine learning and analytics to make inferences about users (donors and fundraisers) to tailor content, and users can opt out.
nonprofit_offer: Built for charities. The Start plan has no monthly fee; card processing and Gift Aid fees apply.
note: JustGiving and your charity are separate data controllers for donor data, so donors' details sit in JustGiving's own system as well as yours. Ask Blackbaud where that data is stored if location matters to you.

name: Enthuse
storage: UK hosting on Microsoft Azure and AWS
plans: All plans
nonprofit_offer: Built for charities. Only Mass Participation (pages for official events such as the London Marathon) has no monthly fee; the other products have a monthly fee. Payment and Gift Aid fees apply.
note: Enthuse says it hosts in the UK and requires two-step verification for all admin users. Check which monthly package you are on, because features and fees differ by product.

name: Stripe
contracting_entity: Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. (contracting entity for UK and EEA); Stripe Technology Company Limited (data controller outside the Americas)
storage: Transferred to other countries, including the US and India.
ai_detail: The privacy policy (updated April 2026) lists training AI models to power services and prevent fraud. Stripe's Payments Foundation Model is trained on tens of billions of transactions across its network. Rights requests go through the Privacy Center.
nonprofit_offer: Lower processing fees for registered non-profits where most volume is donations.
note: Stripe moves your payment and donor data to the US and uses transaction data to train its fraud and payments AI. Two-step login is optional, so an admin should switch on the setting that requires it for the whole team.

name: PayPal
contracting_entity: PayPal UK Ltd (UK accounts); PayPal Giving Fund UK is a separate registered charity (1110538)
storage: Stored in the US and other countries by PayPal's service providers
ai_detail: The UK privacy statement (28 October 2025) says personal data is used to improve services, including improving risk models and developing new products and features. It does not use the phrase AI training.
nonprofit_offer: Charity rate on application for confirmed charities. PayPal Giving Fund enrolment is free.
note: Donations through PayPal Giving Fund go to that fund first, and you only get a donor's name and email if they chose to share them. PayPal stores data in the US.

name: GoCardless
storage: Main processing for European payments on servers in the EEA; some suppliers may transfer data outside the EEA
plans: All plans
ai_detail: GoCardless says its Success+ retry models are trained on millions of recurring payments it has processed, and Protect+ fraud models use data from billions of transactions on its network. The merchant privacy notice (July 2026) says data is used to improve services and for automated fraud decisions.
nonprofit_offer: Charity Pricing plan for registered charities. CICs and companies limited by guarantee without share capital are excluded.
note: GoCardless processes European payments in the EEA and you can move your Direct Debit mandates out through a bulk change. CICs do not qualify for the charity discount.

name: Mollie
contracting_entity: Mollie B.V. (Mollie UK Ltd for UK merchants)
storage: Unknown. Mollie's privacy statement says some processing by third parties may happen outside the EEA. A third-party profile says Mollie commits to storing payment data in European data centres.
ai_detail: The privacy statement (18 July 2026) lists developing, training, using and enhancing automated systems including AI models as a purpose. No opt-out described.
nonprofit_offer: Mollie says it usually offers no discount for charities.
note: Mollie says it usually offers no discount for charities. Mollie treats itself as a separate controller, not your processor, so there is no data processing agreement to sign.

name: Eventbrite
storage: US. Eventbrite says it physically stores personal data in the United States.
ai_detail: The organiser DPA says Eventbrite acts as an independent controller when it uses attendee data for research to improve products and give recommendations. Its sub-processors include no AI provider.
nonprofit_offer: On the Pro marketing plan for verified non-profits. Ticketing fees are not discounted.
note: Eventbrite stores attendee data in the US and can use it for its own product research and recommendations. Eventbrite was bought by Bending Spoons in March 2026, so review the terms again.

name: pretix (hosted)
storage: Germany, on servers in data centres run by German companies
plans: All hosted accounts
ai_detail: The privacy page says pretix does not share customer data with anyone and uses event data only to run ticket sales and calculate its fees. No AI training mentioned.
nonprofit_offer: Lower ticket fee and free tickets for non-profits, on request. pretix decides case by case.
note: pretix hosts all data in Germany and most of its code is open source, so you could run it yourself. Two-factor login is optional, so turn on the team setting that requires it.

name: Ticket Tailor
storage: EU, on AWS in Dublin (Ireland) and Paris (France)
plans: All accounts
ai_detail: Its sub-processors include no AI provider.
nonprofit_offer: For registered charities on proof of status, and a smaller discount for other not-for-profits.
note: Ticket Tailor stores data in Ireland and France, and registered charities can claim half-price fees. Card payments go through your own Stripe, PayPal or Square account, so check those separately.

name: Zettle by PayPal (PayPal Point of Sale)
storage: Unknown. Zettle transfers data to service providers in the US and Australia under Standard Contractual Clauses, and within the PayPal Group under Binding Corporate Rules.
plans: Plan assumed: standard UK pay-as-you-go (1.75% per card transaction, no monthly fee, reader from GBP 29 before VAT for new business users).
ai_detail: Unknown.
note: Zettle is now branded PayPal Point of Sale, so look for either name on your account and invoices. The service is provided by PayPal UK Ltd. Two-step verification is always on: Zettle's help says 'It is not possible to disable 2-step verification on the PayPal Point of Sale account.' Export sales and product reports, and your product library as an Excel file, from my.zettle.com before you close. Ask Zettle how to get your customer list out.

name: SumUp
storage: SumUp says 'for our European business we store our personal data within the European Economic Area'. It may transfer data to group companies and providers outside the EEA and UK. The same policy names SumUp Payments Limited (London) as a data controller 'for our business in Europe'.
plans: Plan assumed: pay-as-you-go (1.69% per in-person card payment, no monthly fee). Payments Plus is GBP 19 a month before VAT, as stated on the pricing page.
ai_detail: SumUp's privacy policy says it develops 'machine-learning risk assessment tools' for fraud prevention and risk management.
note: SumUp says it stores European data in the EEA, not the UK, so check that the wording covers your UK account. Turn on 2-step authentication for the main login: it is optional and codes go by email or SMS. Sales reports export to CSV or Excel from the dashboard. Ask SumUp about a charity rate before assuming one.

name: MobilePay (MyShop, Donations)
storage: Unknown. The data processing agreement allows sub-processors in third countries with safeguards, and the sub-processor list is available on request. Plan assumed: a business agreement for MyShop or Donations.
plans: MyShop and Donations need a business agreement. Donations cost 0.99% plus 1 kr per transaction (checked 2026-10-08).
ai_detail: Plan assumed: business agreement.
nonprofit_offer: Lower donation fees for ISOBRO members. No general non-profit price for MyShop.
note: Ask about the databehandleraftale before you use it for donor data. The published agreement covers only Loyalty and Login. For payments, the merchant terms say you and Vipps MobilePay are each independent controllers. The business portal signs in with MitID, with single sign-on if your organisation has set it up, or with an email and password for older accounts. An administrator adds each user, so name two administrators. A MobilePay Box is for private use only: MobilePay says it may not be used to collect money for an organisation, so use Donations. Settlement and transaction reports download as PDF, Excel (XLSX) or CSV from the business portal.

name: Betalingsservice
job: Collecting membership fees and regular payments by direct debit
storage: Unknown. Mastercard's general privacy notice says data moves within the Mastercard group and may go to the USA and other countries, under binding corporate rules and similar safeguards. Plan assumed: a creditor agreement with a data supplier agreement.
plans: Unknown. Prices are in a separate price list on betalingsservice.dk. Banks also offer Betalingsservice on their own terms.
ai_detail: Unknown.
note: No databehandleraftale is offered. Mastercard Payment Services says it is an independent controller for Betalingsservice, so 'there should be no data processing agreements for these products'. Check how your membership system or bank sends the data, as they may need their own agreement with you. You apply for, renew and sign the agreement with MitID Erhverv. You can end the agreement with one month's written notice; Mastercard Payment Services can end it with two months' notice. An ended agreement cannot be reopened, and ended payment agreements cannot be restored. Ask what you can export and how you would move members to another way of collecting.

name: WordPress.com
storage: US and EU. WordPress.com stores personal data on servers in both the US and the EU and cannot restrict a site to one location. Self-hosted WordPress is different: data lives wherever your web host puts it.
plans: Business plan sites can pick EU West as the primary data centre when hosting features are first activated, but data is still not restricted to the EU.
ai_detail: Automattic licenses public site content to third parties, including AI companies, unless you tick 'Prevent third-party sharing' under Settings, Reading. This applies to public content. Assumed plan: Personal or Premium.
note: WordPress.com shares public site content with AI companies unless you tick 'Prevent third-party sharing' in Settings, Reading. If your site is self-hosted WordPress, ask your web host where the server is.

name: Squarespace
storage: US. Squarespace's privacy policy refers to 'our servers in the US', and its data processing addendum lets it transfer your data to other countries, in particular the US. Customers outside the US contract with Squarespace Ireland Limited.
plans: Plan assumed: any paid plan (Basic, Core, Plus or Advanced).
ai_detail: Squarespace's terms let it use your content to provide and improve the services. Its help page says you can ask known AI crawlers to exclude your site; this is off by default and 'doesn't retroactively remove content previously scraped'.
nonprofit_offer: Enter NONPROFIT at checkout for a discount on your first payment.
note: Your site and contact records are held in the US. Squarespace says it exports only some content: one blog with its posts, layout pages and text and image blocks. Store pages, product blocks, video and audio blocks, styling and custom CSS do not export. Check what you would need to rebuild before you choose it. Two-factor sign-in (passkey, authenticator app or text message) is switched on by each person for their own account, so check every contributor has done it.

name: Wix
contracting_entity: Wix.com Ltd. (Israel) and its affiliated companies
storage: Wix says it stores information in data centres in the United States and Ireland. Wix also uses group companies and processors worldwide.
plans: Plan assumed: any Wix Premium plan.
ai_detail: Wix's Generative AI Policy lists 'User-generated content (such as images and page layouts)' as a data source for its AI models, under a 'License given to Wix in the Terms of Use'. The policy describes no opt-out. Plan assumed: any Wix Premium plan.
nonprofit_offer: On a 2-year Premium plan for TechSoup member charities in listed countries, including the UK and Ireland. Not for Wix Studio plans.
note: Wix keeps data in the US and Ireland. Wix says it uses content you create on its platform, such as images and page layouts, to develop its AI models, and describes no opt-out, so read its Generative AI Policy before you upload personal data. Wix does not offer a full-site export, so export your contacts, products, orders and bookings as CSV files before you cancel. Wix says you can turn on 2-step verification for your account, with no plan limit stated, so check it is on. The discount renews at the standard rate after two years unless you cancel.

name: Shopify
storage: Shopify's data processing addendum says customer personal data may be transferred and processed in any country where Shopify, its affiliates or service providers are located, including Singapore and Canada.
plans: Plan assumed: Basic, Grow or Advanced. Shopify's help says requiring staff to sign in with a secure method is available only on Shopify Plus.
ai_detail: Shopify's terms say Shopify Network Intelligence uses your customer data alongside data from other merchants and from Shopify for Enhanced Services, and you can turn it off in Settings, Customer Privacy. Plan assumed: Basic, Grow or Advanced.
note: Ask Shopify where orders and customer records are kept. You can export products, customers and orders as CSV files from the admin, but check whether your theme, pages and app data come with them. Each person sets up two-step sign-in on their own account, and only Shopify Plus can require it for everyone, so check every staff account has it on. Check whether Shopify Network Intelligence is off if you want it off. Your contract is with Shopify International Limited, in Ireland.

name: Google Analytics 4
storage: Global Google data centres, with no residency option. Traffic from UK and EU devices is collected on UK or EU servers and IP addresses are discarded, but data is then forwarded to Analytics servers for processing.
ai_detail: GA has data sharing settings, including 'Google products & services', which lets Google use your data to improve Google products, and 'Modeling contributions & business insights'. These are chosen at sign-up and can be changed under Admin, Account settings. Assumed plan: free standard GA4 property.
note: Google Analytics sends data outside the UK and EU and keeps detailed data for 14 months at most. Check the data sharing settings in Admin and switch off any you do not need.

name: Plausible Analytics
storage: Germany. Visitor data is stored on Hetzner servers in Falkenstein, Germany, on EU-owned infrastructure.
plans: All cloud plans
ai_detail: Plausible's DPA says it processes visitor data only on the customer's documented instructions, and its data policy says data is not used for advertising, profiling or monetisation. Assumed plan: Starter or Growth cloud plan.
nonprofit_offer: On Business plans with annual billing. Contact Plausible for a code.
note: Plausible keeps your website statistics in Germany with an EU company. You can only export summary figures on normal plans, not raw visit logs.

name: Umami Cloud
storage: You pick US or European Union as the data region when you set up the account. It cannot be changed afterwards.
plans: All cloud plans, if EU is selected at account setup
ai_detail: The privacy policy says Umami does not sell or share personal information, but it says nothing about AI training. Assumed plan: Hobby (free) or Pro.
note: Choose European Union when you set up Umami Cloud, because the data region cannot be changed later. The company is based in the US.

name: Matomo Cloud
storage: Germany. Matomo Cloud is hosted on AWS in Frankfurt, with backups in Dublin.
plans: All Matomo Cloud plans
ai_detail: InnoCraft acts as processor under the Matomo Cloud DPA. Matomo's website privacy policy says its AI providers receive only aggregated reports and may not train general-purpose models. Assumed plan: Business or entry Cloud plan.
note: Matomo Cloud keeps your analytics in Germany. The company is in New Zealand, which the EU and UK treat as having adequate data protection.

name: SurveyMonkey
contracting_entity: SurveyMonkey Inc. (EU entity: SurveyMonkey Europe UC, Ireland)
storage: US by default on AWS. The EU data centre is only available to Enterprise customers.
plans: Enterprise only (per the International Data Center Overview updated 15 April 2025)
ai_detail: The privacy notice says SurveyMonkey uses de-identified response data to train its models, and sentiment analysis and other machine learning features are switched on for all accounts and cannot be turned off. No opt-out from de-identified training is described. Assumed plan: Team Advantage or individual Advantage.
nonprofit_offer: For eligible non-profits upgrading from a free plan, at SurveyMonkey's discretion.
note: On ordinary plans SurveyMonkey stores your surveys in the US, as the EU data centre is Enterprise only. Free accounts cannot export responses or use two-factor sign-in.

name: Typeform
storage: US by default. Typeform's main servers are on AWS in Virginia, USA. EU data hosting is only on Enterprise or Growth Custom plans.
plans: Enterprise and Growth Custom
ai_detail: Typeform's AI FAQ says none of its customers' data is used to train any model. AI-powered insights can be switched off in Admin settings. Assumed plan: Basic or Plus.
nonprofit_offer: NGO discount on monthly and yearly plans, by application.
note: Typeform is a Spanish company but stores your forms in the US unless you are on an Enterprise or Growth Custom plan.

name: Jotform
storage: US by default. You can switch to EU storage in account settings (or use eu.jotform.com); form data then moves to Google Cloud servers in Frankfurt, Germany.
plans: Offered as an account setting.
ai_detail: Jotform's AI policy says personal data is never used to train its AI, but 'data you include in the forms you create, such as in form fields, may be used to train our AI'. No opt-out is described. Assumed plan: Bronze or Silver.
nonprofit_offer: On all annual plans.
note: Jotform stores forms in the US unless you switch on EU storage in your account settings, so check the Data tab. Its AI policy allows form content to be used for AI training.

name: Tally
storage: EU. Tally says it is 'Made and hosted in the EU' and that all form data is encrypted and stored in Europe.
plans: All plans. Two-factor sign-in has no stated plan limit.
ai_detail: Tally's DPA says it processes personal data only on the customer's documented instructions and not for other purposes. The privacy notice separately says Tally may use data you provide to improve the tool. Assumed plan: Free or Pro.
nonprofit_offer: On Tally Pro, for new Pro customers.
note: Tally is a Belgian company and stores form data in the EU. Tally offers two-factor sign-in with an authenticator app, which each person turns on in their own account settings, so check every user has done it. You can download form responses as CSV from the Submissions tab.

name: LimeSurvey Cloud
storage: You choose the server country when creating the instance: Germany, Finland, United Kingdom, USA, Canada or Australia. Data is then stored only in that country.
plans: All Cloud plans, by choosing Germany, Finland or UK at setup
ai_detail: Assumed plan: Basic or Expert Cloud plan.
nonprofit_offer: For charitable organisations on proof of charity status.
note: When you create your LimeSurvey Cloud site, choose the UK, Germany or Finland as the server location. Two-factor sign-in is a built-in plugin you need to switch on.

name: Xero
storage: US by default. Xero says it hosts customer data with AWS on servers in the US, and some EU customer data is processed in New Zealand.
ai_detail: Xero says its JAX assistant does not use customer data to train the LLMs it uses, and its AWS, Azure and GCP model providers do not retain it. Separately, the UK privacy notice says Xero uses personal data to improve services and develop new products 'using AI/ML' and offers no specific opt-out. Assumed plan: Standard or Premium business plan.
nonprofit_offer: For registered not-for-profits, after Xero verifies charity status. Claim within 31 days of subscribing.
note: Xero stores your accounts in the US, not the UK. Export your reports, CSV lists and attachments before you ever cancel, as there is no one-click full backup.

name: QuickBooks Online
storage: Not clearly stated. A UK help article says data is kept on AWS 'in your home country to satisfy data residency laws', but Intuit's UK GDPR page reserves the right to store and process data in the US and other countries.
ai_detail: Intuit's global privacy statement says it may use personal information to improve and develop products 'by training our artificial intelligence models and other machine learning models', and creates anonymised aggregate statistics. No specific opt-out is offered beyond general UK/EU data rights such as objecting to processing. Assumed plan: Simple Start or Essentials.
note: Intuit does not clearly say whether UK accounts are stored in the UK, and it trains its AI models on customer data. Ask Intuit in writing where your data is held if that matters to your trustees.

name: Sage Accounting
storage: Ireland. Sage lists AWS in Ireland as the data hosting location for Sage Business Cloud Accounting.
plans: All Sage Accounting plans
ai_detail: Sage's AI and data ethics principles say it analyses customer product data together with other customers' data 'to develop and train AI models', and that it does not offer a choice on use of anonymised data. Identifiable data is not shared with third parties without permission. Assumed plan: Sage Accounting Standard or Plus.
nonprofit_offer: Through Sage Foundation for registered charities, trusts and non-profits. Check the offer is still live.
note: Sage keeps your accounts in Ireland, inside the EU. Sage uses anonymised customer data to train its AI and there is no opt-out for that.

name: e-conomic
storage: EU. e-conomic says your accounting data is hosted in the EU. Its sub-processor list names Google Cloud (Ireland) for the application and database servers and Microsoft Azure (Netherlands and Ireland) for the database backup. The list also names suppliers outside the EU, such as Twilio SendGrid (USA) for sending email, so read the current list. Assumed plan: any e-conomic package.
plans: Packages are Basis, Plus, Smart and Komplet, from 249 to 649 kr a month before VAT (checked 2026-09-29).
ai_detail: e-conomic's subscription terms let it use your application data 'to maintain, offer, price and develop the Application'. After the agreement ends it may use the data in anonymised form. Assumed plan: any e-conomic package.
note: A databehandleraftale (data processing agreement) is offered on e-conomic's own site, and you can download it from the help centre. Export your data before you cancel. The terms say e-conomic may delete it after the agreement ends, and export is via CSV files. An archive licence keeps data for 5 years if you buy one. Two-factor sign-in (2FA) is required for every user.

name: FreeAgent
storage: Ireland. FreeAgent says it hosts and stores UK client data on AWS servers in Ireland, with backup snapshots in London. Its subprocessor list also names AWS, Google Cloud and DigitalOcean with locations in the US, UK and EU.
plans: Plan assumed: any FreeAgent plan (sole trader, partnership, limited company or landlord). No plan difference is stated.
ai_detail: FreeAgent's Trust Centre says it has internal policies and controls for AI. Its subprocessors include no AI or LLM provider.
nonprofit_offer: For registered charities: contact FreeAgent support with your charity number. Not-for-profits, CICs and social enterprises are considered case by case.
note: FreeAgent stores your accounts in Ireland, with backup copies in London. 2-step verification is optional and uses an authenticator app, so switch it on for every user. Use Export All Data to take a full copy with attachments before you ever cancel. FreeAgent offers registered charities 50% off, but you have to ask support for it. FreeAgent is owned by NatWest Group and is free with some NatWest business accounts, so check what happens to your plan if you close that account.

name: Dinero
storage: Netherlands, with a copy in Ireland. Dinero says it is hosted in the cloud with Google and Microsoft Azure, with files and data physically on servers in the Netherlands, and uploaded files also mirrored on servers in Ireland. Its sub-processor list also names some US-based suppliers (for example Mailchimp and Datadog) and says it uses EU standard contractual clauses where a supplier is outside the EU. Assumed plan: any Dinero plan.
plans: Starter (free, up to 100,000 kr yearly revenue), Starter+, Pro and Total, from 245 to 545 kr a month (checked 2026-09-29).
ai_detail: Dinero's terms let it use your application data 'to maintain, offer, price and develop the Application', and after the user relationship ends only in anonymised form. Dinero's sub-processor list names Microsoft Azure as host of 'databases and AI models' and Visma's SmartScan for reading invoice data. Assumed plan: any Dinero plan.
nonprofit_offer: Dinero Starter is free below a yearly revenue limit, and Dinero says associations can use it.
note: A databehandleraftale is offered. Dinero says it takes effect when you register as a customer, and that continued use after an update counts as acceptance. Two-factor login can be switched on, so check each user has it. Export: postings, account statements and reports download as CSV or PDF, a SAF-T file is available, and contacts and products export as CSV. The paid backup file (495 kr before VAT) holds reports, sales invoices and credit notes, postings and all uploaded bilag that have been posted, as PDF and CSV, one financial year at a time. Dinero says it keeps accounting data for five years after you cancel.

name: Billy (now Shine Regnskab)
storage: EU. Shine's privacy policy says your data is kept on servers with Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services inside the EU, but some data is also passed outside the EU, including to the USA. Its data processing agreement lists Amazon (Luxembourg) and Google (Ireland) and some US suppliers such as Stripe, Intercom and Datadog. Assumed plan: any Billy or Shine Regnskab plan.
plans: Free (3 invoices and 10 expense receipts a month), Basic 160 kr, Plus 295 kr and Complete 595 kr a month before VAT on annual payment; Basic 225 kr and Plus 345 kr on monthly payment (checked 8 October 2026). Complete has a 12-month minimum term.
ai_detail: Shine's privacy policy says your data is not used 'for developing, training or improving AI technologies, except when strictly necessary to deliver our services'. This is the Shine policy, not a Billy-only one. Its terms let Shine use ideas or suggestions you send it, or post in a public area, without compensation. Assumed plan: any plan.
note: Billy is now run under the Shine name, and billy.dk pages for the data processing agreement and terms send you to Shine's pages. A databehandleraftale is offered and counts as signed when you accept the terms. Export before you cancel: the older Billy terms say you must do the export yourself before the subscription ends. Billy's backup is a zip file with a folder for each transaction, converted to PDF with its attachments. Lists such as the posting journal, contacts, products and chart of accounts export separately (CSV, Excel or PDF), so export those too. Ask Shine whether two-factor login is available on your plan. The contracting company for Denmark is Shine Denmark ApS. The privacy policy names Ageras A/S as data controller, and the terms define the Shine Group as Ageras A/S and its subsidiaries.

name: 1Password
storage: Depends on the sign-up site: accounts made on 1Password.eu are hosted in the EU, 1Password.com in the US. Data is never moved automatically between regions.
plans: All plans; choose 1Password.eu when creating the account
ai_detail: Vault items are end-to-end encrypted and 1Password staff cannot read them.
nonprofit_offer: Through the sales team.
note: Make sure your account address ends in 1Password.eu if you want EU hosting, because an account made on 1Password.com is in the US and cannot be moved without starting again.

name: Bitwarden
storage: You pick US or EU in the server drop-down when you create the account or organisation. EU data sits in Microsoft Azure in the EU.
plans: All cloud plans; choose the EU server at sign-up
ai_detail: Vault data is encrypted on the device before it reaches Bitwarden's servers, so it cannot be read for training. No AI training use is described.
note: Choose the EU server when you sign up, because moving from US to EU later means exporting and re-importing everything. Most of the code is open source under GPL and AGPL, with some business features under Bitwarden's own licence.

name: LastPass
parent: Francisco Partners and Elliott Investment Management (private equity owners)
storage: US by default. LastPass also runs vault storage in Europe (Ireland, Germany, UK), used when elected at account creation.
plans: Region is elected when the account is created.
ai_detail: Vault contents are encrypted on the device and LastPass says it cannot read them.
note: Vaults are stored in the US unless Europe was chosen when the account was set up, so ask LastPass which region yours uses. LastPass had a major breach in 2022 that led to a UK ICO fine in 2025.

name: Proton Pass
storage: Proton-owned servers located only in Switzerland, Germany or Norway. There is no customer choice.
ai_detail: Proton Pass data, including metadata, is end-to-end encrypted and Proton says it cannot decrypt it.
nonprofit_offer: On Proton Pass and other Proton services.
note: Your vault may be stored in Switzerland or Norway rather than the EU, although Switzerland and Norway have strong data protection laws. Business plans let admins require two-factor sign-in for everyone.

name: KeePassXC
storage: On the user's own device, in an encrypted .kdbx file. It only goes elsewhere if you put the file in a cloud folder you choose.
ai_detail: The app runs locally and the project says no stored data is ever sent to it or third parties.
nonprofit_offer: For everyone.
note: KeePassXC keeps passwords in a file on your own computer, so data location is wherever you save or sync that file. Decide where it is stored and backed up, and who holds the master password. It has no two-step sign-in in the usual sense: it uses a master password, with an optional key file or hardware key. Answer Yes to two-step sign-in only if you use one of those.

name: Trello
storage: US (AWS data centres). Trello has no data residency option.
ai_detail: Atlassian's data contribution scheme, in force from 17 August 2026, uses metadata and in-app data from Free and Standard plans of Jira, Confluence and JSM for AI by default. Atlassian says it does not apply to Trello because Trello has no data contribution settings. Recheck if Trello gets these settings.
nonprofit_offer: Atlassian Social Impact licence, on Standard, Premium and Enterprise.
note: Trello data is held in the US and there is no option to move it to the UK or EU. Export each board to JSON from time to time, as spreadsheet and full workspace exports need Premium.

name: Asana
storage: US (Virginia) by default. Frankfurt storage is a paid add-on on Enterprise and included in Enterprise+.
plans: Enterprise (paid add-on) and Enterprise+; region Frankfurt, Germany; no UK region
ai_detail: Asana states it does not use customer data for training and its AI partners are contractually barred from doing so. Admins can switch AI features off in the admin console.
nonprofit_offer: On Starter and Advanced for registered non-profits, including outside the US.
note: Asana keeps your data in the US unless you pay for Enterprise with the EU add-on. Only Enterprise plans can force everyone to use two-factor sign-in, so ask staff to turn it on themselves.

name: Notion
storage: US by default. Enterprise customers can choose Frankfurt (EU) for workspace content at no extra cost.
plans: Enterprise only; EU region Frankfurt; no UK region; Notion Mail and Calendar excluded
ai_detail: Notion says it does not use workspace data to train models by default. Sharing is only through the opt-in AI LEAP programme. AI subprocessors are contractually barred from training on customer data.
nonprofit_offer: On the Business plan for eligible non-profits worldwide, after verification.
note: On non-Enterprise plans your Notion content is stored in the US. Two-step sign-in is available to everyone but admins cannot enforce it for members, so ask each person to switch it on.

name: Airtable
storage: US by default. EU storage is only available on Enterprise Scale, and some metadata and login data stay in the US even then.
plans: Enterprise Scale only; EU region; no UK region
ai_detail: Airtable's AI Terms say it will not use or let AI providers use customer data to train generative AI models. On Free, Team and similar plans, providers may keep inputs for up to 30 days for safety checks.
nonprofit_offer: On the Team plan for registered non-profits, including outside the US. Monthly billing only.
note: Airtable stores your bases in the US on the Team plan. Leaving is hard because export is one table at a time as CSV, so keep regular copies and save attachments separately.

name: monday.com
storage: Set by where the first user is when the account opens. Accounts opened from the EU on Standard, Pro or Enterprise go to the EU region (Germany); the UK is not named, and most others default to the US.
plans: Standard and Pro accounts created on or after 23 January 2023, and Enterprise; not Free or Basic
ai_detail: monday.com says it does not use customer data to train AI models and bars its AI providers from doing so. It may access data temporarily, up to 60 days, to improve services and detect abuse; an admin can opt out by emailing ai-support@monday.com.
nonprofit_offer: Free Pro seats for eligible non-profits, with discounts on extra seats and Enterprise. UK Community Interest Companies are excluded.
note: Check Administration, then Profile, to see which region your account is stored in, because it is fixed when the account is created and cannot be moved later. UK charities should not assume EU storage.

name: OpenProject (cloud)
storage: EU. The standard cloud runs on Amazon Web Services with all services in Europe; hosting on EU-owned Scaleway is available on request.
plans: All cloud plans
ai_detail: OpenProject does not run its own AI model. AI use is through its MCP server with a client and model the organisation chooses.
nonprofit_offer: Special rates for NGOs and educational institutions, from sales.
note: Your data stays in the EU, but on a US-owned cloud provider unless you ask for EU-owned Scaleway hosting. Check backup size, as attachments over 1 GB are left out of self-service backups.

name: Zapier
job: Connecting tools and moving data between them
storage: US. Zapier says it is hosted on Amazon Web Services in the United States, and that it does not offer EU-only storage. Zapier also passes your data between the other tools you connect, and each of those tools keeps its own copy.
plans: Plan assumed: Free, Professional or Team. Company and Enterprise differ on AI training.
ai_detail: Zapier's terms say it 'may derive de-identified data sets from your Customer Content' and use them 'to operate, enhance, improve, and develop Zapier products or services, including through model training'. Company and Enterprise plans are opted out automatically; on other plans you opt out with a form. Zapier's security page says it does not train on the data that runs through your workflows, on any plan. Checked 8 October 2026.
nonprofit_offer: On paid plans, after Zapier checks proof of non-profit status from your own country.
note: Zapier moves data between your other tools, such as forms, email lists and accounts, and passes it through US servers on the way. List which tools each Zap touches, and check the settings of each one. Unless you are on Company or Enterprise, fill in Zapier's opt-out form if you do not want de-identified data from your content used for model training. You can export your Zaps and account data, but exporting Zaps is only for Team and Enterprise plans.

name: Canva
storage: US by default. EU storage for designs and media is only offered on Enterprise, Campus and District plans.
plans: Enterprise (and Campus, District education plans); no UK option
ai_detail: Canva says it does not use content to improve AI unless privacy settings allow it, and the default is off. Individual users can opt in or out in Privacy settings. Teams, Business and Enterprise accounts currently cannot opt in. Canva for Nonprofits runs as a team account.
nonprofit_offer: Canva for Nonprofits: Canva Pro and team features for eligible registered charities, with discounted extra seats.
note: Your designs are stored in the US on the Nonprofits plan, and EU storage is only available on Enterprise. Download important designs as PDF or PPTX regularly, because there is no editable export.

name: Adobe Creative Cloud
job: Design, photo and print (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign)
storage: Plan assumed: Creative Cloud for teams. Adobe cloud storage data centres are in Dublin (Ireland) for EMEA, Virginia (US) for North America and Tokyo for Japan, and your geographic region determines where files are stored. The UK is not named. Adobe's privacy policy says its main processing locations for personal information are the US and India.
plans: Creative Cloud for teams (business storage, 1 TB per user, shared across the team). Your geographic region determines where files are stored; it is not chosen by you.
ai_detail: Adobe's General Terms of Use say: 'We will not use your Content to train generative AI models except for Content you chose to submit to the Adobe Stock marketplace.' Adobe also says an account under a business profile, such as a team profile, is automatically opted out of content analysis for product improvement. Plan assumed: Creative Cloud for teams. Checked 8 October 2026.
nonprofit_offer: Individual memberships through TechSoup. For teams, Adobe points non-profits to discounted Education Teams plans.
note: Export: you can download files from Adobe cloud storage on the web and export a whole Libraries collection, or single assets, from the Creative Cloud desktop app; colours, fonts and templates in a library cannot be exported. Cloud documents use Adobe's own formats (PSDC, AIC), so save a copy in a standard format from the app. When a teams licence is cancelled, storage for that licence drops to 5 GB and Adobe says you have 30 days to move anything above that out, after which some or all files may be removed. Ask Adobe in writing which region your team's files are stored in, because the UK is not named. Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign files also live on each person's computer unless saved to the cloud, so check where your team saves them. Nonprofit offers are individual licences through TechSoup; for a team, ask Adobe or a reseller about the discounted Education Teams plans under its VIP buying programme. Adobe offers a data processing addendum for business customers: ask for it.

name: Figma
storage: US by default. Figma's privacy policy says 'All personal information we process is transferred to, processed and stored in the United States, where our headquarters and our main servers are located.' Local file hosting (EU and other regions) is only on the Enterprise plan. Billing information, metadata, logs and file search data stay outside that option.
plans: Enterprise only (localised file hosting, EU among the regions). Plan assumed for the rest: Professional. No UK region.
ai_detail: Figma's help centre says content training is on by default for Starter and Professional teams, and off for Organisation and Enterprise plans: 'By default, content training is turned on for Professional teams.' Team admins can turn it off on Starter and Professional. On Organisation and Enterprise it is currently disabled and cannot be switched on. Plan assumed: Professional.
nonprofit_offer: Figma says it has no non-profit discount. Anyone can use the free plan.
note: On the Starter and Professional plans, content training is switched on by default, so a team admin should check the setting and switch it off if you do not want your files used. Files are stored in the US unless you are on Enterprise. Two-step verification is available on any plan but each person sets it up, and only Enterprise with Governance+ lets an admin require it. You can save a local .fig copy of each file, which works in Figma only.

name: Affinity (by Canva)
contracting_entity: Canva UK Operations Ltd for UK billing addresses; Canva Pty Ltd (Australia) for most other countries, including Ireland and Denmark
storage: Your design files are stored on your own device and the supplier says it cannot access them. A Canva account is needed to download and activate the app. Anything you upload or export to Canva sits in your Canva account.
plans: Plan assumed: the free Affinity app with a free Canva account. AI tools need a paid Canva plan.
ai_detail: The supplier says content in Affinity is not used to train AI features. The Canva AI tools inside Affinity need a paid Canva plan and an internet connection, and content you upload or export to Canva follows your Canva privacy settings.
nonprofit_offer: For individuals.
note: Affinity keeps files on your computer, but you need a Canva account to get and activate it. Check who in your organisation owns that Canva account, and turn on two-step sign-in for it in the Canva account settings. Export: Affinity's help lists PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, PSD, PDF, SVG, EPS, EXR and HDR. Your working files use Affinity's own .af format, so export a copy in a standard format for anything you need to keep long term. If anyone uses the paid AI tools or exports to Canva, check the Canva privacy settings for that content.

name: GIMP
contracting_entity: GIMP team (community project). Donations are handled by the GNOME Foundation as fiscal agent.
storage: On your own device, in the files you save. It only goes elsewhere if you save or share those files to a cloud folder or service you choose.
ai_detail: The app runs on your device and the project says it does not collect, transmit, share or use any personal data. It checks for new versions no more than once a week in some builds.
nonprofit_offer: For everyone.
note: GIMP has no account and no sign-in, so there is no two-step sign-in to switch on. Your images live wherever you save them, so decide where they are stored and backed up. The project says it collects no personal data, apart from a weekly update check in some builds. The US location is the GNOME Foundation that handles GIMP's donations, not a place where your data is held. Export: GIMP saves in its own XCF format, which 'is the only format that can store everything about an image', and exports to a wide variety of formats through File, then Export As (including PNG, JPEG and TIFF; it opens Photoshop PSD files). Keep an XCF copy for editing and an export for sharing.

name: Inkscape
contracting_entity: Inkscape project, a member project of Software Freedom Conservancy (US non-profit)
storage: On your own device, in the files you save. It only goes elsewhere if you save or share those files to a cloud folder or service you choose.
ai_detail: The app runs on your device and the project's privacy policy says the software does not collect or transmit any personal information.
nonprofit_offer: For everyone.
note: Inkscape has no account and no sign-in, so there is no two-step sign-in to switch on. Your logos and drawings live wherever you save them, so decide where they are stored and backed up. Inkscape saves in SVG, an open standard that many other programs can read, and exports to PNG, PDF, EPS and other formats, so you can take your files with you. The US location is the Software Freedom Conservancy, which is the project's legal home, not a place where your data is held.

name: Adobe Express
storage: Unknown. Adobe says Creative Cloud for enterprise applications, including Adobe Express, are hosted in North America, Europe and Japan. Plan assumed: Adobe Express Premium from the nonprofit offer.
plans: Unknown.
ai_detail: Adobe's General Terms of Use say: 'We will not use your Content to train generative AI models except for Content you chose to submit to the Adobe Stock marketplace.' Adobe also says content is never used to train partner AI models offered inside Adobe Express. Plan assumed: Adobe Express Premium (nonprofit offer).
nonprofit_offer: Premium is free for a year at eligible charities and non-profits. After the year, check what Adobe charges.
note: The nonprofit offer is free for one year, so put the renewal date in your diary and check the price then. Ask Adobe where your Adobe Express files are stored. Download finished graphics as a copy outside Adobe. You can download designs as PDF, PowerPoint (.pptx), Photoshop (PSD) and GIF files. Each person turns on two-step verification in their own Adobe account. The offer is for staff only, so it does not cover volunteers unless they are part of your organisation.

name: BrightPay
storage: Bright says its data is 'hosted in European regions', 'in EU/Ireland or UK ISO 27001 certified datacentres', and lists Microsoft Azure, AWS, OVH and Google as hosts. Its support desk (Zendesk) and email delivery (Twilio SendGrid) are in the US.
plans: Plan assumed: BrightPay cloud. Bright says only the cloud version is offered for 2026/27, and BrightPay for Windows was discontinued after 5 April 2026. Price depends on the number of employers and employees, and Bright points to a pricing calculator; monthly or annual billing is offered.
ai_detail: Bright's subprocessors include no AI provider.
note: BrightPay holds payroll and employee data, so ask Bright where your cloud data sits: it says Ireland, UK or EU, not one country. Two-factor sign-in is optional, and an owner or administrator can make it compulsory for every user. Bright's cloud FAQ says you cannot save a file of your payroll data to your computer, but reports can be downloaded as CSV or PDF, so save your reports after each pay run. If you still use desktop BrightPay, check your backup is on your own storage, as that version has ended.

name: Sage Payroll
storage: Ireland. Sage's list of sub-processors names Amazon Web Services (a US company) for data hosting and cloud infrastructure for Sage Business Cloud Payroll, with hosting and processing in Ireland. Some other sub-processors process data in the USA, including Postmark, which sends payslip and pension letter emails. Plan: cloud Sage Payroll.
plans: Plan assumed: cloud Sage Payroll (Essentials, Standard or Premium). Sage 50 Payroll on your own computer is a different product and is not covered.
ai_detail: Unknown for Sage Payroll specifically. Sage's general AI and data ethics page says it analyses product data together with data from other Sage customers to develop and train AI models, where the law allows. Ask Sage whether this applies to your payroll data and whether you can opt out.
note: Payroll holds names, addresses, National Insurance numbers, pay and bank details. You contract with Sage (UK) Ltd unless your invoices name another Sage company. Sage's help says cloud Sage Payroll cannot export all your payroll data at once or take a backup, so run and save your reports (the detailed pay run report can be saved as CSV) after each pay run. Sage does not delete your data for six months after the agreement ends, and may delete it after that. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for everyone who logs in, and each user needs their own login. Ask Sage in writing whether your payroll data is used to train AI.

name: BrightHR
storage: UK for customers who subscribe in the UK. BrightHR says it stores data in the country of subscription, on Microsoft Azure. Irish subscribers' data is kept in the EU.
plans: Plan assumed: any UK subscription (Core HR Software, Enhanced HR Support or Full HR, Health & Safety and Wellbeing). BrightHR does not tie the storage location to a plan.
ai_detail: BrightHR's AI Policy says that for the BrightHR and BrightSafe product it does not use content you input to train, develop or enhance its AI models. It says it may do so for other products.
note: Staff records, absence and documents are kept in the UK when you subscribe in the UK. BrightHR says you can export data at any time through reports (Employees, Absence, Documents). Ask what you would receive on leaving. Two-factor sign-in is available: each user turns it on in My Account using an authenticator app. Contracts run for 24, 36 or 60 months, so check the length and the notice terms before you sign.

name: Breathe HR
contracting_entity: Centurion Management Systems Ltd (trading as Breathe)
storage: UK. Breathe says it uses the AWS London region (eu-west-2), with a failover centre elsewhere in the UK, and that none of your data leaves the UK.
plans: All plans (Micro, Starter, Regular, Pro, Premium, Plus).
