ai_detail: Breathe's AI Assistant policy says 'We do not plan to train base models on customer content.' Breathe holds ISO 42001 (AI management) certification.
note: Staff records are kept in London on Amazon Web Services. Breathe says you can export employee data and download documents yourself. Two-factor sign-in is compulsory for Admin accounts and switched on automatically for HR users. An Admin can require it for everyone in Configure, Settings, Security, so check it is on for everyone who can see staff records. Breathe is owned by an Australian company, ELMO, so check which entity is named on your order.

name: Google Ads (including Google Ad Grants)
contracting_entity: Google Ireland Limited, or Google Commerce Limited where the account's purpose of use is 'eligible non-business use'
storage: Unknown. Google's data processing terms say it "may process Customer Personal Data in any country in which Google or its Subprocessors maintain facilities". Google lists its data centre locations publicly.
plans: Plan assumed: a standard Google Ads account, and the Google Ad Grants account for eligible charities.
ai_detail: Unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Google Ad Grants: free search ads for qualifying non-profits verified through Google for Nonprofits.
note: Google Ads does not tell you one place your data is kept, so check the data processing terms for your account. You can download reports and account data as CSV and other files. Ad Grants is search ads only, and you apply through Google for Nonprofits first. Google "strongly encourages all advertisers to use 2-Step Verification". An account administrator can turn the requirement on or off under Access and security, so turn it on. On a UK account the contract is with Google Commerce Limited if you chose 'eligible non-business use' when you signed up, and otherwise with Google Ireland Limited.

name: Facebook and Instagram
contracting_entity: Meta Platforms Ireland Limited (controller for people in the UK and EEA)
storage: Unknown. Plan assumed: a free Facebook Page, a free Instagram professional (business or creator) account, and the free Meta Business Suite with a Business Portfolio. Meta's privacy policy, which covers Facebook and Instagram, says it shares information across its offices and data centres worldwide, and relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for European data sent to Meta Platforms, Inc. in the US. Meta's Data Processing Terms, which cover its business tools, say Meta may use sub-processors based in the USA, the EU or EEA, or other countries.
ai_detail: Meta says it uses public posts and comments from adult users' accounts on Facebook and Instagram to improve its generative AI models, and that it does not use private messages with friends and family unless someone in the chat shares them with its AI (UK announcement, 13 September 2024; EU announcement, 14 April 2025). UK and EU users can send an objection form.
note: Facebook Pages are run through people's own Facebook logins, so check who holds full control. Aim for at least two trusted people, each with two-step login switched on and recovery details they can still reach. Meta says a Page with nobody holding full control is deactivated and scheduled for deletion.
note_more: Messenger messages from supporters sit in the Page inbox. Meta says a person with full control can download a copy of the Page and choose which categories of information to include. An Instagram professional account is still tied to one login: check who knows the password, which email address and phone number are on it for recovery, and whether two-step login is on. Switching it back to personal disconnects the Page and removes access to ads tools. Instagram's Export your information tool lets you download a profile's data, and messages are among the types of information you can choose. If you use Meta Business Suite, check your Pages and Instagram account are added to the Business Portfolio, not only to one person's profile, and that at least two trusted people have full control. Meta says two-factor authentication is required for some portfolios more than 90 days old, and that only people with full control can require it for everyone. Deleting a portfolio moves its Pages back to a personal profile. Insights can be exported (CSV, PDF or PNG). The portfolio's settings and people list have no export, so note them down. Test a download before you rely on it.

name: LinkedIn Company Page
contracting_entity: LinkedIn Ireland Unlimited Company (controller for people in the UK and EEA)
storage: Unknown. Plan assumed: a free LinkedIn Page. LinkedIn's privacy policy says it processes data both inside and outside the United States and uses legal mechanisms for transfers.
ai_detail: LinkedIn says that from 3 November 2025 it can use some data from members in the UK, EU, EEA, Switzerland, Canada and Hong Kong to train AI models that create content. It names profile details and public content members post, and says it does not include private messages. For UK members the same setting also controls whether LinkedIn shares this data with Microsoft for Microsoft's model training. Members can turn this off in their own settings (Data for Generative AI Improvement), which is on by default. The setting belongs to each member's account, not to the Page.
note: A LinkedIn Page is managed by people's personal LinkedIn profiles. LinkedIn says every Page needs at least one super admin, so check that at least two trusted people hold that role, and that each has two-step verification on and can recover their own login. If the only admin leaves, other people have to request access and current super admins must approve it. LinkedIn says you can "create and export reports for analytics on visitors, content, followers, and competitors" as an XLS file. Check whether you can take out follower lists and Page messages before you depend on it.

name: X (formerly Twitter)
job: Organisation account, posts and direct messages
contracting_entity: X Internet Unlimited Company, Ireland (named Twitter International Unlimited Company in earlier terms; controller for people in the UK, EU and EFTA states).
storage: Plan assumed: a free X account. X's global operations help page says information may be transferred to and stored in the United States, Ireland and other countries, and that X uses Standard Contractual Clauses where they apply.
ai_detail: X's privacy policy says X may share public posts and how you interact with Grok with xAI. X's Grok help page describes a setting under Privacy and safety, Data sharing and personalization, Grok & Third-party Collaborators, to allow or stop your public data and Grok interactions being used for training and fine-tuning. The setting is per account and does not remove data already collected. Privacy policy dated 15 July 2026. Updated Terms of Service take effect 9 October 2026, so check them again after that date.
note: X's terms say the contract for people in the UK, EU and EFTA states is with an Irish company. Check who holds the login: X has a Delegate feature that lets people act for an account with an Admin or Contributor role, without sharing the password. Set it up so at least two trusted people can get in, then turn on two-step login for the main account. Authenticator app and security key are open to everyone; text message codes are for Premium subscribers only, so check which method you are using. You can download an archive of your data (profile, posts, direct messages, media, followers and lists, in HTML and JSON files) from Settings; ask for it before you need it. Check the Grok data-sharing setting on the account, and read the new terms before they start on 9 October 2026. Confirm the Delegate rules and the setting names in the account itself.

name: Bluesky
contracting_entity: Bluesky Social, PBC (controller; representatives named for the UK and EEA).
storage: Plan assumed: a free Bluesky account on the Bluesky-run server. Bluesky's privacy policy says: "We may transfer, process, and store all personal information we collect anywhere in the world." It relies on Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers out of the EEA, UK and Switzerland.
ai_detail: Bluesky's privacy policy and terms (both last updated 14 August 2025) say nothing on training AI with your content. On its own account Bluesky said on 15 November 2024: 'We do not use any of your content to train generative AI, and have no intention of doing so.' It said later that month: 'Bluesky will not train generative AI on user data.' These are public statements, not terms of the contract. Posts, likes, follows and blocks are public by design on the network, so other people and companies can collect them.
note: Bluesky is built on the AT Protocol, which is open source (MIT and Apache 2.0). Anyone can run their own server for an account (a PDS), and an account can move from one server to another, so exit is possible. The move needs care: it needs proof of control of the account, big accounts can hit errors and upload limits, and the guide is written for technical people. You can export your public records from Settings as a CAR file. The file does not hold images or private data; images are downloaded separately through the API, one by one. Two-step login by email code is available. App passwords let a scheduling tool sign in without your main password. Check who holds the password: no team or shared-access feature is documented, so at least two trusted people may need to know the login, kept in a shared password manager. Organisations can apply for a verification badge through Bluesky's form; ask if it is right for you. The promise not to train AI is a public post, not a term of the contract, and your posts are public, so check the AI position yourself.

name: Laptops on Windows 10
note: Free security updates ended on 14 October 2025. Paid extended updates cost US$61 per device for the year to 13 October 2026, then double.

name: Staff's own laptops or phones
note: Personal devices used for work are hard to secure, and hard to wipe when someone leaves.
